title: An Exploration of Sport and Performance Psychology Professionals’ Experiences of Perfectionism
abstract: Sport and performance psychology professionals face diverse demands—teaching, research, consulting, travel, and ethical challenges—that may heighten stress, especially for those with perfectionistic traits. Perfectionism involves setting excessively high standards and harsh self-criticism, with both adaptive and maladaptive outcomes. This study explored how nine sport and performance psychology professionals experience and manage perfectionism in their personal and professional lives, including their work with perfectionistic clients. Thematic analysis indicated five key themes: (a) perfectionism is multidimensional, (b) development and impact is multifaceted, (c) it is a double-sided deal, (d) perfectionism in sport and performance psychology is complex, and (e) personal growth. Participants acknowledged both the benefits and drawbacks of perfectionism, noting its influence on their well-being and relatability with clients. Findings highlight the need for personal and systemic strategies to manage perfectionism, promote adaptive aspects, and support professionals’ mental health in high-performance environments.
